units.title: Unit 1: Reading Literature — Theme, Setting & Point of View

lessons.title: Part 1: Theme & How Setting Shapes Plot and Characters
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Developing Theme & Analyzing Story Elements
lessons.reading: A story’s setting (time and place) often creates obstacles that force characters to make hard choices. Watching how a character responds and grows reveals the theme—the author’s deeper life lesson. When summarizing a story, include only objective facts and key events without personal opinions.

principles.title: Theme & How Setting Shapes Plot and Characters
principles.summary: The setting creates challenges that shape character choices and reveal the theme.

bank.passage: A sudden blizzard trapped Maya at the mountain cabin. With the firewood nearly gone, she shared her heaviest blanket with her younger brother and rationed the warm soup.
bank.prompt: How does the blizzard setting affect Maya?
choices: It forces her to act unselfishly
It makes her forget her brother
It lets her walk to town
bank.answer: It forces her to act unselfishly
bank.explanation: Setting is the time and place of a story, which often creates conflict that tests characters.

bank.passage: Eli practiced his speech every evening despite his stutter. On contest day, his voice trembled at first, yet he finished clearly and smiled with pride.
bank.prompt: What is the main theme of this passage?
choices: Winning trophies is all that matters
bank.answer: Persistence helps overcome hard challenges
bank.explanation: Theme is the deeper life lesson or message about human nature revealed through the story.

bank.passage: In the parched desert town, every family guarded their water barrels. When Lena’s neighbor lost his well, Lena carried two full jugs to his porch.
bank.prompt: Why is the dry desert setting important to the plot?
choices: Water is cheap and easy to find
bank.answer: Scarcity makes Lena’s gift meaningful
bank.explanation: Plot is the sequence of events; a harsh setting raises the stakes of a character’s choice.

bank.prompt: What is the difference between a topic and a theme?
choices: Theme is a full message about life
Theme is just one single word
Topic is the main character’s name
Topic tells where the story ends
bank.answer: Theme is a full message about life
bank.explanation: A topic is a subject like "friendship," while a theme is a complete statement like "true friends stay loyal."

bank.passage: Toby boasted that he needed no map on the forest trail. Two hours later, facing three identical forks in the dim woods, he wished he had listened.
bank.prompt: Which lesson does Toby’s experience teach?
choices: Overconfidence can lead to avoidable mistakes
Maps are useless in the woods
bank.answer: Overconfidence can lead to avoidable mistakes
bank.explanation: Characters often learn a lesson when their flaws clash with the story’s conflict.

bank.prompt: What must an objective summary of a story leave out?
bank.answer: Personal opinions and feelings
bank.explanation: An objective summary states only the key events and facts of a text without personal judgment.

bank.passage: During the power outage, neighbors who rarely spoke gathered on the front steps with flashlights and shared stories until midnight.
bank.prompt: How does the power outage shape the characters?
choices: It causes everyone to move away
bank.answer: It brings distant neighbors together
bank.explanation: A change in setting can disrupt normal habits and bring characters into new relationships.

bank.prompt: Which detail best helps a reader find a story’s theme?
choices: How the main character changes and grows
The page number of chapter one
The font size on the cover
bank.answer: How the main character changes and grows
bank.explanation: Tracking how a character responds to conflict and changes reveals the author’s theme.

lessons.title: Part 2: Contrasting Points of View & Fictional vs. Historical Accounts
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Contrasting Perspectives & Historical Fiction
lessons.reading: Authors contrast different characters’ points of view by showing how each person’s role or background shapes their attitude. Under Ohio standard OH.RL.7.9, readers also compare historical fiction with factual history to see how authors blend real events with invented characters to create emotional impact.

principles.title: Contrasting Points of View & Fictional vs. Historical Accounts
principles.summary: Authors contrast character perspectives and blend historical facts with creative fiction.

bank.passage: Mia stared at the roller coaster with wide eyes, thrilled by the roaring drop. Beside her, Sam gripped the rail and wished he had stayed on the bench.
bank.prompt: How does the author contrast Mia and Sam?
choices: Mia feels excited while Sam feels afraid
bank.answer: Mia feels excited while Sam feels afraid
bank.explanation: Point of view is how a character or narrator sees and feels about events in a story.

bank.prompt: How does a historical novel differ from a history textbook?
choices: It adds invented characters and dialogue
bank.answer: It adds invented characters and dialogue
bank.explanation: Historical fiction combines real historical settings with imaginative characters and emotions.

bank.passage: History record: The 1913 Ohio flood damaged thousands of homes in Dayton. Novel excerpt: Young Clara watched muddy river water swirl past her attic window.
bank.prompt: Why did the novelist include Clara’s attic view?
choices: To show the human emotion of the flood
bank.answer: To show the human emotion of the flood
bank.explanation: Fiction writers use personal perspectives to help readers feel what living through history was like.

bank.prompt: Which pronoun shows a story is told in first-person point of view?
bank.answer: I
bank.explanation: First-person point of view uses pronouns like "I" and "we" because a character tells the story.

bank.prompt: What can a third-person omniscient narrator do?
choices: Know the thoughts of multiple characters
Only speak as one minor character
bank.answer: Know the thoughts of multiple characters
bank.explanation: An omniscient narrator is all-knowing and can reveal the inner thoughts of any character.

bank.passage: Coach Dan saw the rain as a chance to test team grit. However, the groundskeeper worried the muddy cleats would ruin the fresh grass.
bank.prompt: Why do Coach Dan and the groundskeeper disagree?
choices: Their jobs give them different priorities
Both want to cancel the game
bank.answer: Their jobs give them different priorities
bank.explanation: Authors develop contrasting points of view by showing how characters’ roles shape their opinions.

bank.prompt: Why might a fiction writer alter a timeline from real history?
choices: To build dramatic tension in the plot
Because history has no real dates
bank.answer: To build dramatic tension in the plot
bank.explanation: Authors sometimes compress or adjust historical details to tighten pacing and dramatic focus.

bank.prompt: What does a factual historical account rely on most?
bank.answer: Verified primary sources and evidence
bank.explanation: Historical accounts rely on real documents, eyewitness records, and verified evidence.

units.title: Unit 2: Informational Arguments, Clauses & Word Roots

lessons.title: Part 1: Central Ideas & Evaluating Arguments and Evidence
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Evaluating Arguments, Claims & Evidence
lessons.reading: In informational texts, the central idea is the main point the author wants readers to understand. When evaluating an argument, check that the reasoning is logical and that the evidence is both relevant (directly related to the claim) and sufficient (enough verified facts to prove the point).

principles.title: Central Ideas & Evaluating Arguments and Evidence
principles.summary: Strong arguments support a clear claim with relevant evidence and sound reasoning.

bank.passage: Community gardens turn empty city lots into fresh food sources. Studies show neighborhoods with gardens eat more vegetables and report stronger neighbor connections.
bank.prompt: What is the central claim of this passage?
choices: Community gardens benefit health and neighborhoods
City lots should become parking garages
Vegetables only grow on large farms
bank.answer: Community gardens benefit health and neighborhoods
bank.explanation: A claim is the author’s main position or argument that they set out to prove.

bank.prompt: What makes a piece of evidence relevant to a claim?
choices: It directly supports the author’s point
bank.answer: It directly supports the author’s point
bank.explanation: Relevant evidence consists of facts, statistics, or examples directly tied to the claim.

bank.passage: We should extend library hours because my cousin likes blue backpacks and libraries have tall shelves.
bank.prompt: How would you evaluate the reasoning in this statement?
choices: Unsound because the reasons are unrelated
Strong because it cites a survey
bank.answer: Unsound because the reasons are unrelated
bank.explanation: Sound reasoning logically connects evidence to the claim; unrelated details make reasoning weak.

bank.prompt: When is evidence considered sufficient in an argument?
choices: When there is enough to prove the claim
When it has just one guess
When it uses no facts at all
bank.answer: When there is enough to prove the claim
bank.explanation: Sufficient evidence provides enough reliable facts and examples to convince a careful reader.

bank.passage: Honeybees pollinate one-third of human food crops. Without healthy bee colonies, orchards produce far fewer apples, almonds, and berries each harvest.
bank.prompt: What is the central idea of this paragraph?
choices: Honeybees are vital for growing food crops
Apples grow best in cold winters
bank.answer: Honeybees are vital for growing food crops
bank.explanation: The central idea is the most important point an informational text makes about a topic.

bank.prompt: Which source provides the strongest evidence for a health article?
choices: Data from a medical research study
A rumor from an anonymous blog
A joke on a cereal box
bank.answer: Data from a medical research study
bank.explanation: Credible, research-backed data provides strong, trustworthy support for informational claims.

bank.prompt: What is a counterclaim in argumentative writing?
choices: An opposing viewpoint the author addresses
A spelling mistake in the intro
bank.answer: An opposing viewpoint the author addresses
bank.explanation: A counterclaim acknowledges the other side’s view so the writer can refute it with evidence.

bank.prompt: Why should readers check if an author uses biased language?
choices: Bias makes fonts easier to read
bank.answer: Bias can slant facts unfairly
bank.explanation: Bias is an unfair preference that can lead a writer to ignore opposing evidence.

lessons.title: Part 2: Clauses, Sentence Types, Modifiers & Greek/Latin Roots
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Phrases, Clauses, Dangling Modifiers & Word Roots
lessons.reading: An independent clause can stand alone as a sentence, while a dependent clause starts with a word like "although" or "because" and cannot stand alone. A dangling modifier happens when a descriptive phrase is missing the noun it describes. Knowing roots like chron (time), bene (good), and rupt (break) unlocks unfamiliar words.

principles.title: Clauses, Sentence Types, Modifiers & Greek/Latin Roots
principles.summary: Combine independent and dependent clauses clearly, fix dangling modifiers, and decode roots.

bank.prompt: What is an independent clause?
choices: A complete thought with subject and verb
bank.answer: A complete thought with subject and verb
bank.explanation: An independent clause has a subject and predicate and can stand alone as a sentence.

bank.prompt: Which sentence is a compound sentence?
choices: The rain stopped, and the sun appeared.
Because it rained, we stayed inside.
The bright sun warmed the porch.
bank.answer: The rain stopped, and the sun appeared.
bank.explanation: A compound sentence joins two independent clauses with a comma and coordinating conjunction.

bank.prompt: Which sentence contains a dangling modifier?
choices: Walking to school, my backpack felt heavy.
While I walked to school, my backpack felt heavy.
Maya carried her heavy backpack to school.
The heavy backpack sat on the desk.
bank.answer: Walking to school, my backpack felt heavy.
bank.explanation: A dangling modifier lacks a clear word to describe; backpacks cannot walk to school.

bank.prompt: What kind of sentence has one independent and one dependent clause?
bank.answer: A complex sentence
bank.explanation: A complex sentence combines one independent clause with at least one dependent clause.

bank.prompt: What does the Greek root "chron" mean in "chronological"?
bank.answer: Time
bank.explanation: The Greek root "chron" means time, so chronological order arranges events by time.

bank.prompt: What does the Latin root "bene" mean in "beneficial"?
bank.answer: Good or well
bank.explanation: The Latin root "bene" means good or well, as seen in benefit and benevolent.

bank.prompt: What does the Latin root "rupt" mean in "erupt" and "interrupt"?
bank.answer: To break or burst
bank.explanation: The root "rupt" means to break or burst, so an eruption bursts outward.

bank.prompt: Which group of words is a dependent clause?
bank.answer: Although the bell rang early
bank.explanation: A dependent clause starts with a subordinating word like "although" and cannot stand alone.

bank.explanation: A complex sentence combines one independent clause with at least one dependent clause.

bank.prompt: What does the Greek root "chron" mean in "chronological"?
bank.answer: Time
bank.explanation: The Greek root "chron" means time, so chronological order arranges events by time.

bank.prompt: What does the Latin root "bene" mean in "beneficial"?
bank.answer: Good or well
bank.explanation: The Latin root "bene" means good or well, as seen in benefit and benevolent.

bank.prompt: What does the Latin root "rupt" mean in "erupt" and "interrupt"?
bank.answer: To break or burst
bank.explanation: The root "rupt" means to break or burst, so an eruption bursts outward.

bank.prompt: Which group of words is a dependent clause?
bank.answer: Although the bell rang early
bank.explanation: A dependent clause starts with a subordinating word like "although" and cannot stand alone.

lessons.title: Unit 2 Exam: Informational Arguments & Grammar Conventions
lessons.reading: Complete 8 questions testing argument evaluation, central ideas, sentence types, dangling modifiers, and Greek/Latin roots.

principles.title: Central Ideas & Evaluating Arguments and Evidence
principles.summary: Strong arguments support a clear claim with relevant evidence and sound reasoning.

bank.passage: Community gardens turn empty city lots into fresh food sources. Studies show neighborhoods with gardens eat more vegetables and report stronger neighbor connections.
bank.prompt: What is the central claim of this passage?
choices: Community gardens benefit health and neighborhoods
City lots should become parking garages
Vegetables only grow on large farms
bank.answer: Community gardens benefit health and neighborhoods
bank.explanation: A claim is the author’s main position or argument that they set out to prove.

bank.prompt: What makes a piece of evidence relevant to a claim?
choices: It directly supports the author’s point
bank.answer: It directly supports the author’s point
bank.explanation: Relevant evidence consists of facts, statistics, or examples directly tied to the claim.

bank.passage: We should extend library hours because my cousin likes blue backpacks and libraries have tall shelves.
bank.prompt: How would you evaluate the reasoning in this statement?
choices: Unsound because the reasons are unrelated
Strong because it cites a survey
bank.answer: Unsound because the reasons are unrelated
bank.explanation: Sound reasoning logically connects evidence to the claim; unrelated details make reasoning weak.

bank.prompt: When is evidence considered sufficient in an argument?
choices: When there is enough to prove the claim
When it has just one guess
When it uses no facts at all
bank.answer: When there is enough to prove the claim
bank.explanation: Sufficient evidence provides enough reliable facts and examples to convince a careful reader.

bank.passage: Honeybees pollinate one-third of human food crops. Without healthy bee colonies, orchards produce far fewer apples, almonds, and berries each harvest.
bank.prompt: What is the central idea of this paragraph?
choices: Honeybees are vital for growing food crops
Apples grow best in cold winters
bank.answer: Honeybees are vital for growing food crops
bank.explanation: The central idea is the most important point an informational text makes about a topic.

bank.prompt: Which source provides the strongest evidence for a health article?
choices: Data from a medical research study
A rumor from an anonymous blog
A joke on a cereal box
bank.answer: Data from a medical research study
bank.explanation: Credible, research-backed data provides strong, trustworthy support for informational claims.

bank.prompt: What is a counterclaim in argumentative writing?
choices: An opposing viewpoint the author addresses
A spelling mistake in the intro
bank.answer: An opposing viewpoint the author addresses
bank.explanation: A counterclaim acknowledges the other side’s view so the writer can refute it with evidence.

bank.prompt: Why should readers check if an author uses biased language?
choices: Bias makes fonts easier to read
bank.answer: Bias can slant facts unfairly
bank.explanation: Bias is an unfair preference that can lead a writer to ignore opposing evidence.

principles.title: Clauses, Sentence Types, Modifiers & Greek/Latin Roots
principles.summary: Combine independent and dependent clauses clearly, fix dangling modifiers, and decode roots.

bank.prompt: What is an independent clause?
choices: A complete thought with subject and verb
bank.answer: A complete thought with subject and verb
bank.explanation: An independent clause has a subject and predicate and can stand alone as a sentence.

bank.prompt: Which sentence is a compound sentence?
choices: The rain stopped, and the sun appeared.
Because it rained, we stayed inside.
The bright sun warmed the porch.
bank.answer: The rain stopped, and the sun appeared.
bank.explanation: A compound sentence joins two independent clauses with a comma and coordinating conjunction.

bank.prompt: Which sentence contains a dangling modifier?
choices: Walking to school, my backpack felt heavy.
While I walked to school, my backpack felt heavy.
Maya carried her heavy backpack to school.
The heavy backpack sat on the desk.
bank.answer: Walking to school, my backpack felt heavy.
bank.explanation: A dangling modifier lacks a clear word to describe; backpacks cannot walk to school.

bank.explanation: A complex sentence combines one independent clause with at least one dependent clause.
